News.title: Asparagus and ricotta on toast with warm ’nduja
News.content:
Step

Heat 2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil in a frying pan and add 80g ’nduja. Keep the heat low and break the ’nduja down with the back of a wooden spoon. It’s really important that you don’t burn it, just allow it to slowly melt (there will still be some meaty lumps in it).

Sports.title: Southampton manager storms out of press conference with club staff forced to step in after ‘Spygate’ row
Sports.content:
TETCHY Southampton boss Tonda Eckert walked out on his post-match press conference after refusing to answer questions about the club being accused of spying on Middlesbrough.

The German coach kept batting away questions from journalists relating to a Saints analyst allegedly being caught filming a Boro training session in the lead-up to the Championship play-off semi-final.



EFL bigwigs have charged Saints with breaking regulations relating to good faith between clubs.



After a goalless first-leg at The Riverside, Eckert was in no mood to answer the allegations.

And finally the Southampton media officer cut short the terse press conference and the German walked out with one local Boro journalist heard to say: “This is not a good look on your football club!”

Asked what his views were on the allegations, Eckert said: “I think the club has made a statement yesterday evening, and I think that’s all there is to say at the moment.”

And then when asked if the allegations were a surprise to him, he said: “I know that these questions are coming up — but I think we shouldn’t get distracted by the importance of these two big games, and the big games always belong to the players.

“They deserve that and the focus is on them.”

Eckert was then asked if he had to speak to his players about the saga or only to focus on the game.

He said: “Only the last part. Let’s focus on the game. There was nothing to say to them.

“We have a big job at hand and it’s just very important that we use all of our energy to focus on what we need to do on the pitch, and again, I think the players have done that in an outstanding way.”



Eckert was quizzed about his handshake with Boro boss Kim Hellberg — but would only say: “From my side, it’s always the same. I shook hands and wish their manager a good game.”

The Saints boss was pressed whether the alleged spy was acting alone rather than on club instructions.

But he said: “The club made a statement and that’s all there is to say at the moment.”

Eckert continued to bat questions away — refusing to answer when he became aware of the incident and if he was concerned that this could cost them promotion.

Eventually press officer Jordan Sibley had a terse exchange with journalists telling them that the club have already made a statement and Eckert had tried to answer questions.



And after asking “Are there any more questions on the game?” but being barraged with more questions on the spying, he and Eckert stood up and walked out.

More to follow.

Sports.title: ‘Modern football at its worst’ – England stars to be forced to wear special badge on kits at World Cup after Fifa deal
Sports.content:
ENGLAND stars will be forced to wear patches at this summer’s World Cup.

Those featuring at their first summer showpiece will have debut patches stitched into their shirts.





The patches will look similar to those worn by Chelsea commemorating their Club World Cup win.

England are set to have several World Cup debutants this summer.

The likes of Elliot Anderson, Anthony Gordon and Cole Palmer could all feature in the finals for the first time.

Plenty of superstars from other nations will also wear the new accessory.

Lamine Yamal, Michael Olise, Erling Haaland and Rayan Cherki are all set to make their debuts on the world’s biggest stage.

Meanwhile, the entire Scotland team will have to wear the patches as they appear in their first World Cup since 1998.

Cape Verde, Curacao, Jordan and Uzbekistan are all making their World Cup debuts in the newly-expanded tournament.

Haiti, meanwhile, return to the finals after 52 years away – with Iraq back for the first time since 1986.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The patches will become part of future trading card sets when Fanatics take over from Panini as an official tournament partner after the 2030 tournament.

Many fans have been left unimpressed by the innovation.

One posted: “Completely bizarre. Modern football at its worst.”

A second pointed out: “Crazy some nations will have it on all the players”.



And a third claimed: “so dumb, gimmicky, and takes away from the clean look of the kit”.

Another added: “Next they’ll call them rookies for the full US integration”.

Sports.title: Chelsea player ratings: Cole Palmer and Marc Cucurella breathe life into Blues but Andrey Santos a ‘ghost’ vs Liverpool
Sports.content:
Chelsea avoided defeat for the first time in the last seven Premier League matches on a sunny Saturday at Anfield.

But it was the worst possible start for the Blues, with ex-academy boy Rio Ngumoha setting up Ryan Gravenberch for the opener from range.





The Reds didn’t capitalise on their lead, though, and the Blues found their way back into the game through a shambolic piece of Liverpool defending.

Enzo Fernández‘s low free-kick snuck all the way through the bodies in the box and hit the back of the net off the post, with the visitors in the ascendancy when the half-time whistle went.

Chelsea continued their strong showing at the start of the second half, with Palmer finding the back of the net and thinking he’d made it 2-1, only for VAR to rule it out.

Liverpool then had a similar moment, with Curtis Jones finding the back of the net, only for the offside flag to be raised against Cody Gakpo.

Arne Slot‘s side hunted for a winner in the second half, with Dominik Szoboszlai and Virgil Van Dijk both hitting the woodwork to see Chelsea travel back to London with a point.

This is how SunSport Chelsea reporter Lloyd Canfield rated the Blues…

FILIP JORGENSEN – 5

Should’ve done better positionally for Gravenberch’s opener; it was a hell of a strike, but not far from the middle of the goal.

Did make a good save in the second half to deny Szoboszlai from just inside the penalty area, and just about avoided any calamities with the Blues under pressure.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

MALO GUSTO – 3

Was consistently rinsed by Rio Ngumoha on the left for Liverpool, who sent him back to Liverpool Lime Street with feints and dribbles all day long.

Wasn’t close enough to Gravenberch, who had time and space to pick his spot for the opener, and didn’t really improve in the second half compared to Cucurella on the opposite side.

WESLEY FOFANA – 7

Reacted quickly to Enzo Fernandez’s low free-kick to distract Mamardashvili and see the ball into the back of the net.

He was solid defensively too, diving into tackles and marshalling the ineffective Cody Gakpo.



LEVI COLWILL – 6

Really solid in his first start of the season after a horrible ACL injury.

He was good both defensively and in playing the ball out from the back, which the Blues have missed all season.

Gave fans a scare when he seemed to have picked up a knock in the second half, but he played on and did so well with more touches than any other Chelsea player.

JORREL HATO – 5

Has been one of Chelsea’s better performers in this horrible run of form, and was strong again today.

He was booked in the second half for a foul on Jeremie Frimpong, but contributed well defensively and his passing was good too.



MARC CUCURELLA – 7

Looked the most likely Chelsea player to find a goal with some dangerous forward runs in the first half, but his first touch let him down on a few occasions.

He was a constant threat on the left wing for the Blues, and continued to create in the second half, with Liverpool utterly unable to mark the flying Spanish fullback.

MOISES CAICEDO – 7

He scored a belter in the reverse fixture, and played well in this one too.

We know Caicedo as an excellent destroyer in midfield, but today he showed the underrated creative side of his game, with several good dribbles and passes.



He won more duels than any other player on the pitch, too, by a distance.

ANDREY SANTOS – 3

Seemed a little lost in a crowded Chelsea midfield, and couldn’t really get involved in the game at all in either phase of play.

A ghost.

ENZO FERNANDEZ – 6

He was quiet to begin with in the first half, but stepped up again when Chelsea needed him with an unconventional free-kick that found the back of the net.



He could’ve, and maybe should’ve made it two just moments later, but for a good save by Mamardashvili before half-time.

At times, his passing was a little slow when Chelsea were attacking, but they would’ve lost the game without him.

COLE PALMER – 7

He looked a bit more like the Palmer of old in this game, with several clever touches and moments of magic on the right side for the Blues.

He thought he’d given Chelsea the lead in the second half with a tidy finish, only to see it ruled out by VAR for an offside offence by Cucurella.



JOAO PEDRO – 5

Was let down by his first touch in the first half after a good ball into him from Palmer, but generally wasn’t given much service from the players behind him.

He battled well physically with Van Dijk in particular, but wasn’t able to make much happen up top.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

SUBS:

REECE JAMES (ANDREY SANTOS , 63) – 5

Added an element of stability to the Chelsea midfield when they needed it, and was better than Andrey Santos.

He was strong in the duels on his return from injury, and the Blues will be more than pleased to have him back.

Sports.title: Former Arsenal star Aubameyang dropped from Marseille squad after ‘spraying club chief with fire extinguisher’
Sports.content:
PIERRE-EMERICK AUBAMEYANG has been dropped by Marseille after reportedly spraying a club chief with a fire extinguisher.

The French giants’ campaign has faltered since now-Tottenham manager Roberto De Zerbi left the club in February.





Marseille have only won one of their last six matches, of which they lost four.

And that has seen them plunged to seventh place in the Ligue 1 table and at serious risk of missing out on European qualification.

With the team’s attitude and commitment called into question, club bosses reportedly ordered players to sleep at the training ground this week.

According to L’Equipe, however, trouble ensued on Thursday when Aubameyang, 36, led a group of ten players in throwing an impromptu party at the base.

The ex-Arsenal star is said to have sprayed a fire extinguisher over club rep Bob Tahri, his bed and his belongings on the fourth day of the player’s stay at La Commanderie.

Tahri, a former French long-distance runner, had reportedly been at the training ground on behalf of sporting director Medhi Benatia and was tasked with enforcing the curfew.

He is said to have been left furious by the incident and reported it to his superiors.

According to Foot Mercato, the players’ rooms were also left in “disarray”, with sources claiming the atmosphere was “almost reminiscent of a summer camp” when they should have used that time for reflection.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Aubameyang has reportedly apologised to Tahri and claimed he just wanted to “liven things up”.

But the ex-Chelsea star was still dropped from Marseille’s squad ahead of Sunday’s match at Le Havre.

Marseille players have been under fire for over a month and controversial Manchester United reject Mason Greenwood has been a focal point of that criticism.

Greenwood, 24, and his team-mates were all given a damning 0/10 rating after last week’s 3-0 thrashing at relegation strugglers Nantes.



And La Provence branded the forward as “scandalous” and compared him to a circus actor.

This comes after Beye reportedly halted training earlier this week after the ex-England international was claimed to have ignored his instructions.

And L’Equipe reported Greenwood angered club officials after skipping French lessons and mandatory medical treatments.

Sports.title: Middlesbrough 0 Southampton 0: Saints fans taunt Boro with BINOCULARS after ‘Spygate’ row as they come away with draw
Sports.content:
MIDDLESBROUGH should have ripped Southampton to shreds inside their Riverside bear pit.

But they were left thanking their lucky stars they go to St Mary’s for the second leg of this Championship play-off on Tuesday all square





Furious Boro fans created a deafening atmosphere — baying for blood amid the spying saga that broke out ahead of this game.

Kim Hellberg’s side should have been three or four goals up and Tommy Conway had a hat-trick at half-time after a rip-roaring opening 45 minutes where Southampton failed to even venture into the Boro box.



But a series of missed chances and fine keeping from Daniel Peretz kept them at bay, and the Saints almost snatched it late on.

Taylor Harwood-Bellis thumped a header against the bar and then Sam Edozie fired inches wide.

The run-up to this game was overshadowed after a Southampton analyst was caught allegedly snooping and filming a Boro training session from some bushes.

The EFL have since charged Saints for breaking their regulations relating to good faith between clubs.



Angry Boro fans gave the Southampton team coach a hot reception as it pulled into the front forecourt.

They chanted “You know what you are … you cheating b***ards” and a whole volley of some of the finest words from the King’s English!

BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Saints boss Tonda Eckert — a man of few words at the best of times — deflected questions before kick-off, answering them like a politician.

Asked how he would feel if another club spied on his sessions, he said: “When it comes to this stage of the season, it’s not the coaches that win games but players.”



Even an under-fire Prime Minister would have struggled to have batted away that question any better.

Southampton were met by deafening boos as they came out for their warm-up with more minced oaths.

All this did was ramp up what was already an electric atmosphere inside the Riverside.

And if a Saints analyst was spying on Hellberg’s men early on, his information didn’t seem to help on the first set-piece as David Strelec was left completely unmarked to meet a Morgan Whittaker corner.

But he thumped his header over the bar — a huge let-off for the visitors.



Southampton were struggling to get out of their own half as Boro played at a high and aggressive tempo. In the opening 20 minutes alone, they had only managed a grand total of 57 passes.

And they were rocking so much that uncharacteristically they had to resort to playing long balls just to get away from their penalty area.

Saints’ goal lived a charmed life when Whittaker picked the ball up on the turn for Boro and drove forward before firing a left-foot shot inches over.



It was not until the 25th minute that a Southampton player actually ventured into the Boro box and that was only Cyle Larin after fruitlessly trying to beat Dael Fry to a big punt forward from Taylor Harwood-Bellis that was comfortably nodded back to keeper Sol Brynn.

Luke Ayling got the better of ex-Boro man Finn Azaz before whistling a shot from 16 yards over.

And the hosts were denied what should have been a dead-cert opener by a brilliant piece of Harwood-Bellis defending.

Whittaker burst past Ryan Manning and Nathan Wood on the right side of the box before pulling back for Tommy Conway.

But the Boro man took a touch before seeing his effort blocked by the Saints defender.



And incredibly Southampton survived again as Riley McGree put the ball on a plate for Conway — who rattled the right post with a first-time finish. The irony was on this occasion he had time to take a touch.

The Boro striker should have had a hat-trick but Peretz managed to get down to keep out his shot from 12 yards.

Southampton will have been delighted to go in at half-time level and after the break they managed to keep the ball more than they did in the entire first half.

They managed to start getting the ball into the Boro box and Larin had a great chance to put them in front but he headed wide from an excellent cross from Tom Fellows.

Eckert decided to bring on former Sunderland striker Ross Stewart to a chorus of predictable boos from the home fans.



Boro fans were getting jittery as they have seen so many times their team dominate, fail to take their chances and then get hit by a sucker blow.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

With six minutes left, Harwood-Bellis powered a header from a Manning free-kick against the bar.

And then Edozie was played in by Shea Charles but shot just wide.

Sports.title: Liverpool 1 Chelsea 1: Fernandez’s fluke strike ends Blues losing streak but woeful Reds pile more pressure on Arne Slot
Sports.content:
WHAT a strange, entertaining afternoon at Anfield.

For a decent spell, only one team played like they were worthy of qualifying for the Champions League, and it wasn’t Liverpool.





And if you had been asked which was the crisis club toiling under an interim manager, you would not have picked Chelsea.

Finishing in the top five may yet earn Arne Slot another season to get it right. But this was another display which raised questions whether he should.



Despite taking an early lead through Ryan Gravenberch‘s stunning shot, Liverpool lacked conviction, composure and basic skills like defending set-pieces and tracking runners.

Instead it was Chelsea who broke their own bad habits. They recovered from the set-back, equalising through Enzo Fernandez‘s weird free kick, and played with a confidence and purpose not seen for weeks in the Premier League.

Ironically, ending the run of six league defeats may actually harm the Blues’ faint hopes of reaching the Champions League by the backdoor.

They need Aston Villa to win the Europa League and finish fifth in order for sixth place to be enough.



On this evidence, you would back Villa to finish ahead of the Reds, even with the distraction of a continental final.

For more than two decades, these clubs have contested crucial end-of-season games.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The highlights reel of Champions League semi-finals, title race twists, top-four shootouts and cup finals documents one of the most compelling rivalries of the era. But this game felt different, in the build-up at least.

Chelsea had blown their chances of a top-five finish. Liverpool were hanging on in there for Champions League qualification after defeat by Manchester United underlined how poor their title defence had been.

The makeshift line-ups added to the sense of two teams trying to pick up the pieces of disappointing seasons.



Florian Wirtz joined Mohamed Salah on Liverpool’s injury list, Alexander Isak was fit enough only for the bench, and Curtis Jones continued his stint in the problem right-back position.

Despite injuries to all four senior wingers and five changes from the dismal defeat by Nottingham Forest, Chelsea still could not find a starting place for £30million striker Liam Delap.

Instead, interim boss Calum McFarlane pushed Marc Cucurella up to the left of the front three behind top scorer Joao Pedro, and it proved to be a masterstroke.

Levi Colwill was also impressive on his first start since his ACL injury, which was further good news ahead of next weekend’s FA Cup final against Manchester City.

Given all the uncertainties, the fast, open start was a pleasant surprise. Pedro shot just wide before Liverpool took the early lead.



Former Chelsea academy star Rio Ngumoha laid the ball into Gravenberch, who took one touch to open up the chance and a second to belt it into the net.

It was a fine strike, but replays suggested Blues stand-in goalkeeper Filip Jorgensen should have done better.

Reds captain Virgil Van Dijk was soon involved at both ends. First, with a brave header to stop Pedro reaching Malo Gusto’s cross. Then with a volley from a Dominik Szoboszlai cross, which he should at least have put on target rather than over the bar.

McFarlane said he wanted his team to show a stronger mentality in the face of set-backs, and they did, taking control of the game.



A trademark Cole Palmer turn and cute pass put Pedro through, only for Giorgi Mamardashvili to come smartly off his line.

The Georgian had to be sharp twice more, pushing away Cucurella’s shot from a narrow angle and then claiming the ball when the Spaniard ran behind the Liverpool defence again.

But the Blues got their reward in farcical circumstances. Fernandez clipped in a free-kick from way out and it went all the way in off the post, with Wesley Fofana claiming he helped it on its way.

Whatever the truth, it was wretched defending by the Reds. The home team were totally on the ropes, and Mamardashvili made a good save from Fernandez, who was rightly disappointed in himself.

Liverpool stumbled through to half-time, but were almost behind soon after it.



Palmer put the ball in the net but Cucurella had been fractionally offside in the build-up.

The Spaniard was running riot and only a well-timed Alexis Mac Allister challenge saved the Reds again. It seemed to wake the home team up a bit

Jones headed into the net but Cody Gakpo had been offside, then Jorgensen made a decent save from Szoboszlai.



The Dane was living dangerously at times with the ball at his feet, but getting away with it.

There were boos when Slot chose to bring off Ngumoha, rather than the ever-ineffective Gakpo, in favour of Isak.

Szoboszlai, Liverpool’s player of the season by a country mile, hit a fierce shot from distance that beat Jorgensen but not his right-hand post.

It was anyone’s game by now. Pedro fired off target, then Van Dijk hit the crossbar with a header from a corner.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Liverpool survived a late claim for a penalty for Jeremie Frimpong’s challenge on Pedro.



In the end neither side quite deserved to win. But Chelsea showed the greater improvement and Liverpool earned the mild boos that greeted the final whistle.

Sports.title: Arne Slot loudly BOOED by Liverpool fans after bringing on Alexander Isak in controversial substitution vs Chelsea
Sports.content:
LIVERPOOL boss Arne Slot was booed by his own fans after bringing off Rio Ngumoha for Alexander Isak.

The teenage prodigy started Liverpool’s 1-1 draw against Chelsea at Anfield and impressed on the left wing as he assisted Ryan Gravenberch‘s opener.





But he was hauled off by Slot in the 67th minute as he brought £130million singing Isak.

And the substitution didn’t go down well with the Reds faithful after the Dutchman took off the team’s main bright spark.

Supporters looked furious as Ngumoha trudged off the pitch amid increasing pressure on Slot’s position.

There were loud whistles from the crowd and some took to social media to vent their frustration too.



One wrote on X: “The Anfield crowd booed Arne Slot for taking off Rio Ngumoha and honestly, they had every right to.

Another said: “You desperately need a goal and the solution is removing your best player? Genuinely absurd.”

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

A third added: “Anfield booing Ngumoha coming off and rightly so. I genuinely cannot believe it.”



And one commented: “Isak wasn’t the problem, Slot took off our positive attacking spark that could’ve played balls into Isak, weird sub…”

The sub certainly seemed strange given that Ngumoha won more duels (6), made more ball recoveries (5) and completed more take-ons (4) than any other Liverpool player.

Liverpool look set to finish in the top five and secure Champions League football, but Slot is still under fire after a disappointing campaign.

Slot was the name on everyone’s lips a year ago after winning the Premier League title.

But the team have given a poor title defence despite spending almost £450million in the summer transfer window.



Liverpool have failed to win their last two games after drawing to Chelsea, which ended the Blues’ dismal winless run of five games.

Enzo Fernandez struck late to secure a point for Calum McFarlane’s men in the first half.

Chelsea thought they had won it before Cole Palmer’s strike was ruled out by VAR, while Liverpool also had a goal from Curtis Jones disalllowed.

Sports.title: Man Utd rocked by triple blow ahead of Sunderland clash with Sesko and Casemiro both OUT
Sports.content:
CASEMIRO will be able to say farewell to Manchester United supporters, despite his absence for the fixture at Sunderland.

The 34-year-old is not in the matchday squad for the first time all season through injury.





United sources say Casemiro was not ready for the trip to Wearside but will recover for the visit of Nottingham Forest next Sunday.

The Forest game will mark Casemiro’s final Old Trafford appearance before he is released at the end of his contract.

Fellow defensive midfielder Manuel Ugarte is also absent at Sunderland after he sustained a “problem in training”.

Ugarte would have deputised for Casemiro if fit but Mason Mount is expected to line up next to Kobbie Mainoo in central midfield.

Mount last started in January and the Sunderland match marks his first start under head coach Michael Carrick.

Striker Benjamin Sesko has also missed out, as expected, with a shin injury he aggravated in the 3-2 victory against Liverpool last week.



Carrick has made five changes to the United side after they qualified for the Champions League last week.

Speaking to United’s club media ahead of the game, Carrick said: “Ben’s (Sesko) been carrying a shin problem for some time, and he took another quite big bang on it.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“Obviously he had to come off last week, so he wasn’t ready today.

“Cassy (Casemiro), he’ll be fine for next week, it’s nothing major.



“Manu (Ugarte) had a problem with his back in training, so that’s the issues kind of ironed out.”

United are making their first trip to Sunderland since April 2017.

Carrick was an unused substitute on that occasion as goals by Zlatan Ibrahimovic, Henrikh Mkhitaryan and Marcus Rashford fired the Red Devils to victory.

A triumph on Wearside on this occasion could virtually guarantee the Red Devils a top three finish.

Sports.title: Arne Slot BOOED by Liverpool fans as Reds fail to beat Chelsea - 5 talking points
Sports.content:
Arne Slot BOOED by Liverpool fans as Reds fail to beat Chelsea - 5 talking points

LIVERPOOL 1-1 CHELSEA: Ryan Gravenberch fired the hosts in front early in proceedings but Enzo Fernandez levelled for the Blues before the break

View 6 Images Arne Slot was booed by Liverpool fans during their draw against Chelsea (Image: Ryan Browne/Shutterstock)

Chelsea finally ended their losing run as the Blues came away from Anfield with a draw - much to the chagrin of Liverpool's fans.

‌



The Kop made their voices heard when Arne Slot replaced Rio Ngumoha with Alexander Isak in the second half as they saw the Reds fail to get the better of Chelsea.

‌



Ryan Gravenberch fired the hosts ahead in sublime fashion early in the piece, curling past Filip Jorgensen in the Chelsea goal from the edge of the box.

‌



But Enzo Fernandez's cross, which may or may not have taken a touch from Wesley Fofana on the way through, levelled for Chelsea before the break.

The Blues had a goal ruled out for offside in the second half but the match ended in a draw, which drew more boos from the home support. Here are five talking points from Anfield...

1. Grav some of that!

View 6 Images Gravenberch curled past Jorgensen in the Chelsea goal (Image: Peter Byrne/PA Wire)

‌



Only five minutes had passed when Liverpool took the lead, and it came from a curious situation. Dominik Szoboszlai, all of 40 yards from goal, lined up a free-kick.

Such is his ferocious power, Chelsea took it seriously and formed a wall which ultimately blocked the Hungarian's ambitious effort.

But the ball broke free to the right and Ryan Gravenberch collected it on the edge of the area before curling a sumptuous strike past FIlip Jorgensen in the Chelsea goal.

‌



It was an eye-catching strike, but the Swede will be disappointed when he sees the replay. Gravenberch caught it well but it's not near the corner, and Jorgensen should have been able to get across.

2. Fofana's golden touch... or was it?

View 6 Images Fofana got the slightest of touches to Fernandez's cross (Image: Chelsea FC via Getty Images)

As the first half went on, Chelsea got stronger and stronger and were well worth their leveller. Enzo Fernandez's free-kick was swung on from the right, doubtless as a cross, but looked to have crept all the way in to restore parity.

‌



But Wesley Fofana swung a leg at it and wheeled away as if he had scored the equaliser, but in his celebration clearly told Fernandez the goal was his.

However, some forensic TV analysis appeared to show Fofana did indeed get a touch before the ball nestled in the bottom corner, although the goal is, as yet, still being credited to Fernandez.

The Argentine was central to Chelsea's fightback in the first period and could have put the Blues in front shortly afterwards. He sprung the Liverpool defence between Curtis Jones and Ibrahima Konate but his powerful effort was saved by Giorgi Mamardashvili.

‌



3. Blues' VAR woe

View 6 Images Palmer thought he had put Chelsea in front (Image: Chelsea FC via Getty Images)

Chelsea thought they had gone in front early in the second half, only for VAR to intervene on the tightest of offside calls.

Marc Cucurella was a constant threat on the Blues' left and was played in to centre a cross which ricocheted off Virgil van Dijk into Giorgi Mamardashvili.

‌



The ball then came out to Cole Palmer who couldn't miss from close range as the Chelsea fans behind the goal rejoiced.

However, despite the lack of flag, VAR adjudged Cucurella to have been offside from the initial pass. The semi-automated technology showed his shoulder narrowly in front of the deepest defender Curtis Jones.

4. Kop make themselves heard

View 6 Images Ngumoha was replaced by Isak

‌



It's fair to say the number of discerning voices towards Arne Slot have grown over the course of the campaign at Anfield, and they made their feelings clear in the second half here.

The Dutchman decided to take off the lively Rio Ngumoha for Alexander Isak on 67 minutes to a chorus of boos from those on the Kop and in other home areas. And the boos were loud and unmistakeable.

Ngumoha has already established himself as a fan favourite at Anfield despite his tender years with his industrious performances and Reds fans probably thought Cody Gakpo was a more suitable candidate to be replaced for the final throes.

‌



5. Two sides at a crossroads

View 6 Images Interim Chelsea boss Calum McFarlane (Image: Ryan Browne/Shutterstock)

It's not far-fetched to think we could see a new face in both dugouts for these two teams come August.

It would have seemed unthinkable when Arne Slot led Liverpool to the league title last year, but this result leaves them a whopping 17 points behind pace-setting Arsenal who also have a game in hand.

‌



Liverpool should retain their place in the Champions League, but the same cannot be said of Chelsea. They sit ninth going into the remainder of this weekend's top-flight fixtures, nine points behind fifth-placed Aston Villa.

Even sixth is starting to look fanciful, which could be enough for a spot at Europe's top table if Villa win the Europa League and stay in their current league position.

But interim boss Calum McFarlane does have an FA Cup final against Manchester City to look forward to next week.

Sports.title: Liverpool fans make feelings clear to Arne Slot with furious reaction to Chelsea decision
Sports.content:
Liverpool fans make feelings clear to Arne Slot with furious reaction to Chelsea decision

Liverpool manager Arne Slot made a substitution with the score at 1-1 against Chelsea, only to receive immediate negative feedback from the Anfield crowd and not get the desired impact

View 2 Images Arne Slot took off Rio Ngumoha

Arne Slot was booed by the Liverpool supporters after deciding to substitute Rio Ngumoha against Chelsea. The Reds were level at 1-1 when Slot brought on Alexander Isak for the 17-year-old winger at Anfield.

‌



Ryan Gravenberch put the home side ahead early on with a curling effort before their lead was cancelled out when Enzo Fernandez's free-kick drifted in at the far post. With the fans getting irritated by the performance as Liverpool faced a side who had lost their previous six Premier League matches, Slot made a call.

‌



He replaced Ngumoha with Isak in the 67th minute and immediately knew what the fans felt about it. Boos rang out around Anfield as the arrival of the big-money summer signing off the bench went down very badly.

‌



"You don't hear a reaction like that at Anfield often, but I can understand," Ally McCoist said on TNT Sports. "I actually thought it would've just been a straight swap for Cody Gakpo, but I know he can play out on that left-hand side and come in off the left as well."

The move didn't work out as Slot had hoped, with the game ending 1-1. To make matters worse, the Liverpool supporters then delivered another volley of boos at the full-time whistle.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Ngumoha has been a bone of contention between the fans and Slot this season. The young winger has been a bright spark when he has featured, but the Liverpool boss has been reluctant to over-play him.

Slot was delighted by his impact in the 2-0 win over Fulham last month and explained his take on the situation of managing his minutes - and expectations.

"I think I’ve said a few weeks, maybe months ago, one or two months ago, that his playing time would increase because he got stronger and stronger, showed more and more when he came in, but also in training sessions, that it wasn’t only a nice trick, but there was more and more end product to what he did," he said.

‌



View 2 Images The substitution didn't go down well

"There was more and more power to what he did, which is needed if you play against the best defenders in the world. And I don’t think anyone is surprised that at this moment of time he scored his first goal [at Anfield].

"He has such a special quality which you don’t see a lot in football anymore: dominating the one-v-one situation. And that’s exactly what he did when he scored his goal, making the ball free by twisting and turning and then hitting it in like a Mo Salah finish, I would say.

‌



"It’s something I’m not surprised to see because in training sessions during the last month we saw more and more that he got more and more power to hit the ball as powerful as he did today.

"And yeah, that’s why he had now three starts in the last seven or eight games, I think. I don’t know exactly, but Wolves and Tottenham and this one. Pleasing to see that he did what we know makes him special, that’s dominating one-v-one situations."

Sports.title: Matt Le Tissier hits out at cancel culture as he rages at Sky Sports sacking again
Sports.content:
Matt Le Tissier hits out at cancel culture as he rages at Sky Sports sacking again

Matt Le Tissier was sacked by Sky Sports in 2020 after voicing his opinions on the Covid-19 pandemic and the Black Lives Matter movement and remains unhappy about it

View 2 Images Matt Le Tissier has spoken about his departure from Sky Sports (Image: Julian Finney/Getty Images)

Matt Le Tissier has hit out at "wokeism" and cancel culture while once again claiming that his personal views saw him lose his job at Sky Sports. The former Southampton midfielder was sacked by the broadcaster in 2020 after voicing his opinions on the Covid-19 pandemic and the Black Lives Matter movement.

‌



The 57-year-old has previously claimed that he was simply "questioning the narrative" around Covid by posting on social media. In 2022 he retweeted a post suggesting the Bucha massacre in Ukraine was staged - an incident which saw him dropped by Southampton as an ambassador.

‌



Le Tissier continues to share his alternative views, with an argument he had with X's AI bot Grok about 'chemtrails' recently going viral. And while he has been branded a conspiracy theorist by some, he has been welcomed back by Southampton and gets work on the after-dinner speaking circuit.

‌



He insists he has no regrets over his departure from Sky Sports, where he was a regular on Soccer Saturday, but the way it happened clearly still irritates him.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Horse racing meeting called off after outbreak of highly contagious disease confirmed READ MORE :

Piers Morgan makes feelings clear as Bruno Fernandes beats Declan Rice to individual award READ MORE :

"I’ve always been fairly opinionated. I’ve always kind of been my own man and able to make my own decisions and have my own thoughts," he told The Telegraph. “And it’s costly. It cost me my job at Sky and anyone who tries to tell you different doesn’t really know what they’re talking about. But I’d do the same again.

‌



“There aren’t many things I’ve regretted. We’re all human and we all make mistakes. You apologise, you correct it and you move on. If you’re on the government side and you f*** up, that’s fine. But on the side I was sat, nobody will accept your apology. You’re cancelled.

“I’m quite happy plodding along. I do my after-dinner speaking, which I’ve done for the last 20-odd years since I retired, although a few years ago people were trying to get me cancelled from jobs there.

View 2 Images Matt Le Tissier used to be a regular on Sky Sports (Image: Bryn Lennon/Getty Images)

‌



"Because I said something about Covid or Black Lives Matter they didn’t think that I should be able to have a job speaking at football clubs about my football career. That’s cancel culture.”

Speaking in 2022 about his departure from Sky, Le Tissier said: "I went into working in the media from 2002 onwards until late August 2020, which was an interesting scenario where I lost my job. Obviously the pandemic started in 2020 in March - and very early on in that I had my doubts as to what was really going on.

"I felt early on there was a massive overreaction to it by the governments. And that's where it all started for me with questioning the narrative and probably ended up with me losing my job at Sky."

Article continues below

Le Tissier now goes on speaking tours with his ex-Sky co-stars Charlie Nicholas, Phil Thompson, Jeff Stelling and Paul Merson and knows there is no way back onto our screens. "I’ll never work in television again in terms of mainstream stuff," he admitted. "That doesn’t bother me."

Sports.title: Marseille 'tired' of Mason Greenwood as ex-Man Utd star fined for behaviour
Sports.content:
Marseille 'tired' of Mason Greenwood as ex-Man Utd star fined for behaviour

Mason Greenwood has been fined by Marseille and is said to have a broken relationship with sporting director Medhi Benatia, with the club growing frustrated with the ex-Manchester United forward

View 2 Images Ex-Manchester United forward Mason Greenwood (Image: Getty Images)

Marseille are becoming 'frustrated' with Mason Greenwood's 'lack of effort' and even 'basic gratitude' in another alarming revelation about the former Manchester United forward.

‌



Greenwood, 24, joined Marseille in 2024, signing a five-year deal after United agreed to offload him for a sum of around £27million. Since his switch to France, the England international has delivered some eye-catching statistics, netting 47 goals and providing 16 assists across 79 outings.

‌



Yet it's his conduct away from the pitch that has sparked concern, with Marseille becoming irritated with Greenwood for not having sufficient commitment and failing to show gratitude, according to L'Equipe.

‌



Cristiano Ronaldo backed to play at 2030 World Cup despite retirement vow READ MORE :

Luke Littler sends clear Man Utd transfer message after Real Madrid statement READ MORE :

It's claimed that Greenwood has stayed in a 'world of his own', unwilling to participate in French lessons required by the club as English is used in the changing room. Club officials are 'tired' of attempting to explain matters to him, even resorting to fines in a bid to alter his attitude.

There is now reportedly a club-wide divide emerging, and his relationship with sporting director Medhi Benatia has deteriorated, with the two men said to be 'completely ignoring' each other daily. Greenwood is believed to be anticipating the inevitable conclusion before an exit, but that isn't expected to be 'straightforward'.

Marseille had hoped to turn a profit from a future sale of Greenwood, but his value has dropped owing to his inconsistent performances in the second half of the campaign. A return to the Premier League is thought to be out of the question for Greenwood, though there is reported interest from Serie A and La Liga.

‌



View 2 Images Mason Greenwood is said to have been punished (Image: Getty Images)

Greenwood's last goal came in a 1-0 victory over Toulouse on March 7, and he endured a difficult outing in a 3-0 thrashing at relegated Nantes in their most recent fixture. He was relegated to the bench for a home clash against Nice last month, fuelling speculation that he has had a falling out with head coach Habib Beye.

Beye, however, dismissed such rumours, insisting that Greenwood has been hampered by a minor injury. "Mason we have looked at since the start of the week, he is very limited by the injury from Lille," Beye said. "It's been two games that he's played with a lot of pain, we can't put him in danger."

Article continues below

Marseille and Greenwood are next in action when they make the trip to Le Havre on Sunday, in what is a pivotal fixture for the club as they bid to secure European football for next season.

Sports.title: Arsenal tactics called out as NBA star claims they 'won't make Champions League final fun'
Sports.content:
Arsenal tactics called out as NBA star claims they 'won't make Champions League final fun'

Arsenal will face PSG in the Champions League final with the Premier League underdogs in the eyes of many - with an NBA star claiming they employee negative tactics

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta's has guided Arsenal to the final of the Champions League - but their methods are not for everyone (Image: Getty Images)

NBA star Victor Wembanyama has claimed that he'll be cheering for PSG in the Champions League final later this month - and fired a dig at Arsenal, who would "not make it fun".

‌



The Gunners made their first European Cup final in two decades by seeing off Atletico Madrid on Tuesday, securing a 1-0 victory on the night and a 2-1 win on aggregate. It was a cagey affair between two teams who are better known for their defensive qualities.

‌



Nevertheless Arsenal remain unbeaten in the tournament to date, a period of 14 games, but their final opponents PSG will provide the toughest test yet. The Parisians are defending champions and downed the Gunners in the semi-finals 12 months ago.

‌



PSG have been relentless in the knockouts, playing some sensational football to knock out Chelsea, Liverpool and Bayern Munich. They have a style that is effective and highly entertaining with Wembanyama backing them to win - and to ensure the game isn't boring.

He said on Amazon Prime Sport: "PSG of course, at least they’re going to make it fun, cause I know Arsenal ain’t".

Two players will miss West Ham vs Arsenal as title race intensifies after Mikel Arteta update READ MORE :

Piers Morgan makes feelings clear as Bruno Fernandes beats Declan Rice to individual award READ MORE :

Arsenal did get the better of PSG last year in the league phase before they clicked into gear, winning home and away against the Premier League side in their last four tie. Mikel Arteta though believes Arsenal can do a job on them what it comes to the showdown in Budapest.

‌



He said: "It is what it is. We knew the level of the opposition that we had to face, either way, Bayern Munich or PSG. We know the quality that they have, and that's it. But obviously, we're also very confident that when we get to that moment, we're going to deliver what we need to."

View 2 Images San Antonio Spurs star Victor Wembanyama has fired a dig at Arsenal's style of play (Image: Amazon Prime Sport)

Steven Gerrard claimed in the aftermath of the semi-finals that Arsenal would go into the final as underdogs, but needed to lean on their physicality and success from dead ball situations if they were to claim continental glory.

‌



He said: "They're playing against a high quality team, an elite manager, Arsenal will have to be the best version of themselves for the full game. Every single player's going to have to turn up, but of course they've got a chance. I think they'll be the underdogs which might suit them.

"If they can win the Premier League it'll give them immense belief and confidence going in. I think they have to use their physicality, their size. They'll need to make every set piece count and take PSG where they don't want to go and make it uncomfortable for them, but they've certainly got a chance."

Sports.title: Boro & Saints tie in the balance after first-leg stalemate
Sports.content:
Middlesbrough and Southampton played out a goalless draw to leave their Championship play-off semi-final finely poised at the midway point.

Boro dominated the majority of the first leg at the Riverside Stadium, dominated in the build-up by the 'SpyGate 2' allegations but couldn't find the breakthrough.

The Saints had some big opportunities late on, but couldn't find a goal either. Just like the other tie between Millwall and Hull, we head into the second leg as we were.

Second leg on Tuesday night The second leg is live on Sky Sports Football from 7.30pm on Tuesday night; kick-off 8pm.

Pre-match overtaken by 'Spygate 2' allegations

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Tonda Eckert and Kim Hellberg both fielded questions about the alleged 'spygate' incident ahead of the crucial play-off semi-final between Middlesbrough and Southampton

Kim Hellberg was not pulling any punches in his pre-match interview, after Southampton were charged with a breach of EFL regulations after a member of staff was alleged to have spied on Boro's training ahead of their play-off tie.

"Possibly?!" the Boro boss said to Sky Sports before kick-off when the allegations were put to him.

"It's not affected our build up. We have done what we should have done before this type of game. We've watched every Southampton game there is, trying to find solutions to beat them - how they press, how they build up. Putting every hour towards getting the advantage to win, in the right way.

"We're motivated. We're going to do everything we can to win the game. It's a new game. I believe in my players. We're going to try to win the game fair."

But after the game, Hellberg was more bullish - accusing Southampton of cheating in his post-match press conference.

When asked about the incident, Saints boss Tonda Eckert walked of his own press conference when too many questions were made about 'Spygate 2'.

Boro dominate first half but can't break through

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Middlesbrough were a tiny margin away from turning their first half dominance over Southampton into a goal when Tommy Conway struck the upright

And to be fair to Hellberg, the first half was pretty much a 45 minutes that summed Boro up. Intense, energetic, creative, but just no end product.

"I can't remember a game as one-sided as this between two sides at the top end of the table," Jobi McAnuff said on Sky Sports at half-time. "They'll be so disappointed they didn't score."

Daniel Peretz's goal was peppered at times, but they couldn't find a way through. Seventeen shots on goal, just four on target. An xG of 1.39 to Southampton's zero.

The best chances fell to Tommy Conway, who had two huge ones in a matter of moments. The first was blocked on the line by James Bree, the other rattled the far post as he tried to bend it into the far corner.

A frustrated Boro boss Kim Hellberg added: "We were outstanding in the first half against a very good football team. That is one of the best halves I've seen since I've been here.

"But you have to score and get momentum from that. The second half was even. They maybe have one chance that feels bigger than ours. That is football. I'm so proud of the players and the supporters. So proud over 90 minutes."

Saints spurn late chances to win

Image: Tom Fellows of Southampton is challenged by Riley McGree of Middlesbrough

It felt like a big opportunity gone for Boro, as the Saints improved after the break, going close themselves twice late on.

First, Taylor Harwood-Bellis headed onto the woodwork from a Ryan Manning free-kick, and then substitute Samuel Edozie raced through on the counter-attack, but fired just wide of Sol Brynn's goal.

From being dominated for most of the clash, the Saints could easily have ended up taking a lead into the second leg.

"The boys were outstanding today," Southampton boss Tonda Eckert told Sky Sports. "It was an excellent performance that will give us so much confidence going into the game on Tuesday.

"I didn't see it that way [being fortunate to go in level at half-time]. We played a very good 90 minutes and had the bigger chances especially towards the end.

"We knew that we were up against a good side, especially at home with their supporters. We knew they would have a lot of energy.

"They used up a lot of it in the first half and we knew the game was going to open up for us later on. We made some small adjustments just like we always do. We adapted quite well and there was more than one chance to win the game."

Saints lucky Boro were in wasteful mood

Image: Tommy Conway missed three big chances to give Boro a precious play-off lead

Analysis by Sky Sports' Laura Hunter:

This first leg was less spy thriller more dry documentary. The build up to the game proved far more entertaining than the action itself. Southampton will consider themselves the big winners, pummelled in a one-sided first half that produced chances galore but no goals.

They rallied in the second but only generated mild threat. Everything ended up with a rating of PG.

In theory, that should ensure Tuesday's return leg is full throttle. No holding back. Boro will be kicking themselves they are not carrying an advantage given they generated 21 efforts at Southampton's goal - four landed to Tommy Conway and he missed three big chances overall.

To break completely with recent form, Saints couldn't muster a single shot on target and looked like a side whose off-field distractions had got the better of them. Tonda Eckert talked up the performance post-match but the only thing that would have pleased him was surely the generosity of the scoreline.

The German has got three days to figure out why his team looked so laboured for much of a game of this magnitude. Perhaps his analyst team have got some extra insight they can offer - that is if they weren't too busy watching Boro, of course.

Sports.title: England ready to 'step up' as World Cup preparations begin against New Zealand
Sports.content:
Charlie Dean says England can "set our standards" for their big home cricketing summer when they face New Zealand in the first ODI match of the multi-format series as preparations ramp up for the Women's T20 World Cup.

England will play their first international of 2026 at Chester-le-Street on Sunday, live on Sky Sports Cricket, when they host the White Ferns in the first of three ODI matches.

Three T20 matches then follow from May 20 to complete the New Zealand series before England then face India at the end of the month in three more T20s. The World Cup starts next month, with England hosting Sri Lanka at Edgbaston in the tournament opener on June 12.

Dean, who captains the side for the three ODIs in the absence of Nat Sciver-Brunt who is not playing on precautionary grounds due to a minor left calf tear, is keen they start on the right foot against New Zealand.

"It would be brilliant for us to kick off with a win," said Dean.

"I guess it would set our standards as to how we want to go about playing this summer.

"They're off the back of a couple of really good series. They played South Africa and won in some high-scoring games out there. So, we knew that it's going to be a challenge and with a young group it feels like a really good opportunity for us to step up and show what we're made of."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The England Women's T20 World Cup squad has been announced

Sunday's match marks England's first international since semi-final defeat to South Africa in the Women's World Cup in October in the 50-over format.

"Following on from the ODI World Cup in October it feels like a fresh start for us maybe in this format," said Dean.

"There's obviously some new players into the squad and potentially some debuts in the horizon which feels really exciting.

"But we've definitely got one eye on the World Cup. Obviously we now know the squads for that T20 World Cup so a lot of girls will be probably focusing a little bit on practising and making sure that we're ready come June 12.

"It's brilliant that we've got a lot of cricket between now and then playing some really brilliant teams, obviously New Zealand and then India coming across. So lots of cricket between now and then and just keeping our skills up to scratch and really working hard to be ready for June 12."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Charlotte Edwards reflects on the 'tough decision' to not select Tammy Beaumont in England's T20 World Cup squad, but insists there is still more to come in her international career

On playing without Sciver-Brunt, Dean said: "It's a bit of a loss for us not to have Nat around. She's here training and around the group which is brilliant.

"But it was just a bit too much of a push for her to play in three 50 overs. But she should be good to go for the rest of the summer, which is great."

England are without Mahika Gaur (foot fracture) and Alice Capsey (illness) for the ODI matches.

"I guess a little bit of a depleted squad but one that's really ready to come up against some real good challenge from the New Zealand squad," added Dean.

"We're excited to get the international summer started and really hit the ground running."

All 12 group matches at the Women's T20 World Cup involving England, Scotland, Ireland, plus the final, will be available to watch without subscription via Sky Sports App.

Sports.title: 'Greatness!' - Wembanyama delivers masterclass as Spurs lead Timberwolves
Sports.content:
Victor Wembanyama delivered another masterpiece with 39 points, 15 rebounds and more game-wrecking defense for the San Antonio Spurs, who took a 2-1 lead in the second-round NBA playoff series with a 115-108 victory over the Minnesota Timberwolves.

Wembanyama went 13 of 18 from the floor and 10 of 12 from the line, adding five blocks and a full night of paint deterrence as the Spurs won their second straight game after dropping the opener at home.

De'Aaron Fox scored 17 points, and Stephon Castle had 13 points and 12 assists with a team-high plus-17 rating.

Anthony Edwards had 32 points and 14 rebounds and Naz Reid added 18 points and nine rebounds for the Wolves, whose defense kept them alive after a woeful start but allowed the Spurs to shoot 6 for 10 from 3-point range in the pivotal third quarter.

Minnesota will host Game 4 on Sunday night. The series shifts back to San Antonio for Game 5 on Tuesday.

Jaden McDaniels drew Wembanyama's fifth foul with 6:18 left and brought the Wolves within 99-98 on a pair of free throws, but the Spurs never trailed in the second half despite never leading by double digits.

Wembanyama didn't flinch despite the foul risk, finishing with 16 points in the fourth quarter. His 3-pointer that answered Reid's pushed San Antonio's lead to six with 3:06 to go. Reid tried another one near the end of the shot clock on the next possession that hit the rim and Wembanyama rebounded.

Edwards, who showed Minnesota yet again his swift healing ability by returning from a deep bone bruise in his hyperextended left knee after just one week to make the start of the series, had 22 points in the first half to help them snap back from an early 18-3 deficit.

"It was like holding the ship together. We had a lead. We didn't need to rush. We needed to be consistent," Wembanyama said.

But it was Wembanyama, 22, who stole the show. Asked what they were witnessing after such a performance, team-mate Fox replied: "Greatness.

"We all know that. We see him every day. We see the work and the time that he puts into his game and his body knowing that teams are going to come out here and try and be physical with him.

"He fights through that, he doesn't complain. He knows what he's going to endure. He comes out here and he produces."

Knicks move to brink of Eastern Conference final

Jalen Brunson scored 33 points and sealed the game with big buckets late to the delight of roaring Knicks fans, leading New York to a 109-94 win over the Philadelphia 76ers on Friday night for a 3-0 lead in the Eastern Conference semi-finals.

Game 4 is Sunday in Philadelphia.

Brunson shook off a 2-of-8 start from the floor and finished 11 of 22 in 38 minutes to send the Knicks to their sixth straight postseason victory.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mitchell Robinson with a huge play in the New York Knicks' win over the Philadelphia 76ers as he dunks over Joel Embiid

"I'm Linus. Jalen's my blanket," first-year Knicks coach Mike Brown said. "He helps me relax at a lot of different times during the course of the game."

With 2016 and 2018 Villanova national championship banners hanging in the rafters, the so-called Nova Knicks all took turns taking the fight out of the Sixers in the fourth quarter, turning a four-point lead into another double-digit victory.

Josh Hart had 12 points and 11 rebounds and Mikal Bridges added 23 points, pushing the Knicks within one victory of their second straight conference finals appearance.

Sports.title: 'I think that says something about you' - McIlroy sends blunt LIV message
Sports.content:
Rory McIlroy has questioned why players would not want to return to play on the PGA Tour amid uncertainty over the future of LIV Golf, bluntly saying "if you don't want to play here, I think that says something about you".

Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) confirmed last month that it will end its funding for LIV Golf at the end of the 2026 season, with the breakaway league now searching for alternative long-time investment to secure its future.

Speaking after he surged into contention at the Truist Championship on Friday with a second-round 67, McIlroy was asked for his take on the LIV situation and the potential pathways back for players to the established tours.

"It's a question if they do want to come back," said McIlroy.

"Obviously we have seen the quotes over the last few days. And, you know, it seems like some of the guys, if... again, it all depends on what happens to LIV.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Rory McIlroy hit a 393-yard drive after bouncing along the cart path during the second round of the Truist Championship

"If it is a scenario where they have the option to come back and play on the traditional tours, I think [PGA Tour CEO] Brian Rolapp has said anything that makes this tour stronger, anything that makes the DP World Tour stronger, I think everyone should be open to that.

"That's just good business practice.

"But again, I think there's going to be a lot of sort of bridges to cross to get there, just because, you know, obviously the guys over there are under contract and if they are able to keep it going and get a schedule together next year, it seems like those guys are still going to play the majority of their golf on LIV, in whatever form it takes."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports reporter Jamie Weir explains what is next for LIV golfers after Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) confirmed it will end its funding at the end of the 2026 season

McIlroy, originally an arch critic of the LIV breakaway in 2022 before subsequently softening his stance, added: "I was probably too judgemental with the guys that went because I was seeing it from my point of view and maybe not seeing it from other points of view.

"I'm not going to judge anyone for not wanting to play on the PGA Tour.

"I don't know, does that mean that they go play DP World Tour, maybe; if that's a pathway, that would make the DP World Tour stronger, and I would be delighted with that because that's my home tour at the end of the day.

"But If you want to be the most competitive golfer you can be, this is the place to be. And if you don't want to play here, I think that says something about you."

Image: Rory McIlroy agrees 'everyone should be open to that' if LIV player returns will make the established tours stronger

McIlroy also took aim at LIV's hope of survival under different backing.

"It's never been for me and, look, it doesn't mean that LIV is going to go away," he added.

"They're going to go and try and find alternative investment, whatever that may look like.

"But when one of the wealthiest sovereign wealth funds in the world thinks that you're too expensive for them, that sort of says something."

'It's really if the players want me back' - what have leading LIV golfers said about future?

Sky Sports understands that several LIV players have sounded out both the DP World Tour and PGA Tour over the possibility of being reinstated.

Speaking earlier this week, Bryson DeChambeau - one of LIV's biggest names - said he will focus on his YouTube channel if LIV Golf fails over a potential return to the PGA Tour.

"I think, from my perspective, I'd love to grow my YouTube channel three times, maybe even more," DeChambeau, who has 2.69m subscribers on the streaming platform, told ESPN.

"I would love to. I'd love to do a bunch of dubbing in different languages, giving the world more reason to watch YouTube. And then I'd love to play tournaments that want me."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jon Rahm explains the agreement he has reached with the DP World Tour regarding his return from LIV Golf

In later comments, DeChambeau said on a potential return to the PGA Tour: "It's really about whether the membership wants me back and if they just want me back. That's what it's about.

"I don't even think it's Brian Rolapp or anybody like one of the top executives, it's really if the players want me back and if not, then I understand that."

Jon Rahm, whose LIV contract runs beyond this season, said of the series' future: "As the future of the league goes, I think that's obviously a question for the business people. We want to be here. It's been a lot of fun. I want to keep competing. I want to keep sharing some time with them.

"But only time will tell. Scott [O'Neil, LIV's CEO] and his team have a lot of hard work to do, but obviously, they're experienced in the area, and that's why they've been chosen to take this role."

Sports.title: Mudbir headlines the Victoria Cup at Ascot
Sports.content:
We have a busy day’s racing on Saturday with action from Ascot, Hexham and Lingfield, live on Sky Sports Racing...

2.20 Ascot - Progressive Mudbir contests big-field cavalry charge

A cracking edition of this ultra-competitive seven-furlong Carey Group Victoria Cup at Ascot sees Mudbir top the betting for John and Thady Gosden.

A progressive son of Kingman, he made giant strides as a three-year-old, winning on three occasions from five starts, and heads here with a huge chance under Oisin Murphy. He was a little unlucky when only seventh as the 11-4 favourite at Goodwood in August and should go close if fit enough on his return from a 259-day break.

Defence Minster is one of several dangers for Hamad Al Jehani and James Doyle. He scored on his first start having undergone a gelding operation at Kempton in March and must defy a four-pound rise as he switches to the turf.

The Kevin Phillipart de Foy-trained Shiplake arrives seeking a hat-trick after winning a pair of all-weather events at Southwell and deserves a crack at this better grade.

1.58 Lingfield - Unbeaten Maho Bay takes on Maltese Cross

A potentially informative renewal of this William Hill Lingfield Derby Trial Stakes where Maho Bay headlines six runners.

Charlie Appleby's son of Dubawi is a perfect two from two after winning on debut at Kempton before making an impressive reappearance when sauntering clear of a decent field at Newmarket. He takes another step up the ladder here but warrants plenty of respect, with further improvement likely over this additional distance.

Aidan O'Brien has claimed this race on seven occasions and Isaac Newton is his representative under Ryan Moore. He brings in plenty of experience but will need to build on his recent fourth behind Morshdi (runs in the Dee) if he is to claim this.

Bay Of Brilliance stepped forward from his first outing to win at Goodwood before following up in emphatic fashion at Recar. Up in class, he looks is a big player for Ralph Beckett and Hector Crouch.

1.28 Lingfield - Appleby's Romantic Symphony bids to remain unbeaten

Well-bred Romantic Symphony headlines a classy field for this Listed William Hill Oaks Trial Fillies' Stakes at Lingfield.

The Charlie Appleby-trained daughter of Dubawi is related to top-class pair Yibir and Wild Illusion and puts her unbeaten record on the line under William Buick. Having landed a Newmarket novice, she defied a penalty to win at Kempton on her return, and this imposing type should continue to improve.

Aidan O'Brien is double-handed with Bloom and Cameo, the pick of Ryan Moore. The latter showed a useful level as a two-year-old and made a satisfactory return when fifth at the Curragh. That was over a mile, and she steps up in distance and back in class.

Bloom made most when third behind Thundering On at Navan and is another who should strip fitter, while Amora Queen and Prizeland complete the quintet.

Ascot - Gosdens have plenty of chances.

Sports.title: McIlroy surges into contention with second-round 67 at Truist
Sports.content:
Rory McIlroy heated up on the back nine on Friday at Quail Hollow to move into contention at the Truist Championship, his four-under 67 seeing him pull within four shots of leader Sungjae Im.

Playing his first tournament since winning The Masters for a second year running, McIlroy was one under and eight shots back when he made the turn, before back-to-back birdies at the 10th and 11th got him rolling.

McIlroy added further birdies at 13, 15 and 16, though he'd end his round with a bogey as his par putt on 18 lipped out after he'd found a greenside bunker.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Rory McIlroy hit a 393-yard drive after bouncing along the cart path during the second round of the Truist Championship

"It was a good day to get myself back in the hunt, and feel like I have a real chance going into the weekend," McIlroy said. "I started to make some good swings, especially with the irons."

Image: Tommy Fleetwood is just one shot off the lead after two rounds of the Truist Championship

McIlroy isn't the only big name in contention. Tommy Fleetwood shot 67 for the second straight day to trail leader Im by one shot.

Justin Thomas, who won the PGA Championship at Quail Hollow in 2017, is two back, along with PGA Tour newcomer Alex Fitzpatrick - Matt Fitzpatrick's brother - who continues his bright start since earning his tour card after their victory at the Zurich Classic of New Orleans.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the fourth round of the Zurich Classic of New Orleans at TPC Louisiana in Avondale

Rickie Fowler, meanwhile, vaulted into the mix with the day's low round, an eight-under 63, which included nine birdies. He, like McIlroy, is four shots off the pace at five under.

Cameron Young, a two-time winner on the PGA Tour this year, shot 70 and is five strokes back.

For Im, the South Korean followed an opening seven-under 64 with a 69 as he looks for his first tour win since 2021 in Las Vegas.

"I know this course very well, so I'm taking advantage of that," Im said. "And then the scrambling, because of the play with the Presidents Cup, I know where to miss the greens, I'm very familiar with this golf course. But I didn't putt very well today, but I'm happy with where I'm at."

Chandler Blanchet had the shot of the day, a hole-in-one on the par-three 17th. It was the fourth ace at 17 in tournament history and the first since Mark Hubbard in 2023.
